title: [Bug][SM120] MTP speculative decoding acceptance rate drops to 0% on nightly with native FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE_SM120 backend (GLM-5.3-Flash)
bodyExcerpt:
## Environment
- vLLM: `0.30.1rc1.dev539+g5b6b657e1` (nightly wheel, 2026-10-02 build, commit `5b6b657e1`)
- Hardware: 8x RTX PRO 6000 (SM120), PCIe, no NVLink
- Model: GLM-5.3-Flash (FP8 checkpoint, TP=8)

- Base image: vllm-openai v0.30.0 + nightly wheel force-reinstall (no-deps)

## Observed behavior
MTP speculative decoding drafts tokens but the acceptance rate is **exactly 0%** — every drafted token is rejected. Decode speed falls back to non-speculative baseline (~80 tok/s vs ~163-190 tok/s with working MTP).

SpecDecoding metrics from server log (eager mode, spec_tokens=3, 512-token essay generation):

All three legs rule out graph-mode interaction and multi-step draft-forward as the cause.

title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Expand indexer block tables when kernel blocks span several storage blocks
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fixes the sparse-attention indexer reading the wrong cache slots on GLM-5.3-Flash/ROCm once a sequence exceeds 2048 tokens (the dense-shortcut threshold). The indexer block table is in kernel-block units (1152 tokens), but the compressed indexer cache is paged in smaller storage blocks (128 tokens). The builder only converted the table when the kernel block was *smaller* than the storage block.

## Claims

- Fixes corrupted sparse top-k selection beyond 2048 tokens for GLM-5.3-Flash on ROCm (MI355X), in both prefill and decode.
- Restores GPQA-Diamond accuracy from 80.8–85.4% (with degenerate, non-terminating generations) to 89.9–91.4%. This matches the pre-regression baseline.
- No behavior change when the kernel block size equals the storage block size or divides it (the existing path). That covers NVIDIA, DeepSeek-V3.2 and every model that doesn't set `storage_block_size`.

## Validation

Unit tests (`tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py`):

- `test_to_storage_block_table`: CPU-only checks of the conversion helper. It covers no kernel block size, equal sizes, kernel smaller than storage (the existing collapse) and kernel larger than storage (the new expand).
- `test_indexer_builder_expands_kernel_blocks_to_storage_blocks`: builds the indexer metadata with a 1152-token kernel block over a 128-token / `tokens_per_state=4` storage spec. It checks every prefill compressed slot and every decode block-table entry against slots computed independently.

```
python -m pytest -q tests/v1/attention/test_indexer_deepseek_v4_slot_mapping.py
# with fix:    33 passed
# without fix: 5 failed (the new tests), 28 passed
```

End to end, GLM-5.3-Flash on MI355X, TP=2:

Decode-vs-prefill consistency. For each sequence, I generate greedily, then re-score the same tokens with a single prefill. "Gap" is the mean |logprob(decode) − logprob(prefill)| over the first 64 generated tokens. "Flips" is the share of positions where the argmax differs.

title: [Bugfix][GLM-5.3] Size the image encoder cache from the exact token ceiling
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fixes #59539. `Glm5NextProcessingInfo` inherits GLM-4V's square most-features probe, which reaches only 7921 of the processor's 8000 token budget, so ordinary non-square images (a 4032x3024 phone photo, a 3840x2160 4K frame, an A4 scan) were refused with HTTP 400 at serving time.

## Claims

- `get_image_size_with_most_features()` now returns an aligned canvas whose grid factors the token ceiling exactly (8000 -> 2240x2800) instead of the nearest aligned square (2492x2492).
- Encoder cache sizing and the profiling dummy both cover the real per-image worst case through the existing code path; `mm_processor_kwargs={"max_pixels": ...}` overrides keep flowing through `_get_image_max_pixels`.
- No behavior change for images that already worked. Only the 7922-8000 token band goes from rejected to accepted.

## Validation

```
PYTEST_DISABLE_PLUGIN_AUTOLOAD=1 .venv/bin/python -m pytest tests/models/multimodal/processing/test_glm5next.py -q

title: [Bugfix][Rust Frontend] Preserve whitespace in GLM string arguments
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

The Rust GLM tool parser removes leading and trailing whitespace from generated string arguments before returning them as tool calls. A tool receiving `"    return 1\n"` gets `"return 1"`. For coding agents, this can change written code or break whitespace-sensitive edit matching even when the model supplied the correct text. Preserve the original string, as the Python GLM parser already does after [#42026](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/pull/42026).

For example, an edit targeting the complete line `"    total = 1\n"` can instead match inside `subtotal = 10` once the whitespace is removed. The reproducer below shows the parser turning an intended `total = 2` edit into `subtotal = 20`.

**Scope:** This defect was isolated directly in the Rust parser while investigating GLM verification failures. Any model using the Rust frontend's `glm45` or `glm47` tool parser can encounter it when generated string arguments contain leading or trailing whitespace. Both parsers share the affected XML value parser, so the fix applies across models using either parser, for complete and streaming input. Other Rust parsers and the separate Python frontend are outside this patch.

## Claims

- Preserve string arguments in the Rust `glm45` and `glm47` parsers, for complete and streaming input.
- Keep schema-based numeric conversion; the reproducer's `" 2 "` still becomes integer `2`.

## Validation

CPU reproductions against bases `aee8fe202a2f` and `3a6963664537`; the full parser-crate suite was rerun on the submitted patch based on the latter:

| Check | Before | After |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Full-line edit, GLM-4.5 / GLM-4.7, complete / 7-byte chunks (4 combinations) | Changes the wrong variable; returns 21 | Changes only the target line; returns 12 |
| Integer argument in those calls | `2` | `2` |
| Separate indented-code insertion, same 4 parser/chunk combinations | `IndentationError` in all 4 | Valid code returning 7 in all 4 |
| Two new regression tests | Both fa

title: [Bugfix][HiSparse] Reject cudagraph_mode=FULL at startup
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

HiSparse cannot capture prefill or mixed batches in CUDA graphs. It picks its prefill path from per-step page residency (resident pages, or spilled pages staged from host), and it mirrors prefill KV to host outside the graph. With `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a backend reporting `ALWAYS` support (FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100) has prefill/mixed batches captured as FULL graphs. A replay could then take the branch frozen at capture and skip the host mirror.

## Changes

HiSparse rejects `cudagraph_mode=FULL` at config validation, next to its other unsupported-config checks (PP, DCP). The error points to `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE` (the default), which keeps FULL graphs for decode batches. Being a config check, it covers every backend HiSparse runs on.

Separately, `FULL` with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100 currently crashes on prefill replay even without HiSparse: #59681.

## Test Plan

- New `test_hisparse_rejects_full_cudagraph_mode` in `tests/test_config.py`.
- B200, shrunk GLM-5.3 (dummy weights), `FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`, `cudagraph_mode=FULL`, a small pool so prefill context spills to host: TRTLLM ragged and FlashAttention prefill.

## Test Result

- The new test fails without the change; `tests/test_config.py -k hisparse`: 13 passed.
- B200, before: `FULL` + HiSparse crashed in both runs: a mixed active/empty query rows error with TRTLLM ragged prefill, an illegal memory access with FlashAttention prefill. Now it fails at startup with the error above.

AI assistance (Claude Code) was used for this PR.

title: [Bugfix][Structured Output] Feed the token that implicitly ends reasoning to the grammar
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Structured output skipped a reasoning-end token that is also content, such as GLM's `<tool_call>` with no `</think>` before it. The grammar then forced a second `<tool_call>`, and `required`/named tool calls were lost. This PR feeds that token to the grammar, which matches what `extract_content_ids` already does. Fixes #59608.

## Claims

- The grammar now consumes a reasoning-end token that `ParserEngine.extract_content_ids` keeps as content, if the grammar accepts it. Close tags such as `</think>` are still skipped.
- On GLM-5.3-Flash, the doubled-`<tool_call>` signature went from 7/40 (`required`) and 8/40 (named) to 0/40 in both modes. The same holds with MTP speculative decoding: from 9/40 and 11/40 to 0/40.
- Under speculative decoding, the mask row at a drafted `<tool_call>` stays unconstrained, so a draft cannot force the end of reasoning. When `<tool_call>` is the last draft, the bonus row is now masked from the grammar state after it.
  - The unit case `inclusive_last` covers this. Its bonus row equals the row after accept, and the grammar then rejects a second `{`. It fails without the fix on both backends.
  - A CPU check of the scheduler flow, `spec_bonus_row_check.py` (`logs/fix_spec_bonus_row_check.log`), shows the same for `<tool_call>` as the last draft, the only draft, a mid-window draft and the recovered token.
  - End to end, the live MTP run went from 9/40 and 11/40 signatures on stock to 0/40 with the fix. Draft acceptance was 58.5% with the fix and 59.1% on stock.
- The same failure reproduces on Qwen3 (`qwen3` + `hermes`), and the fix removes it there too.
- This does not raise the rate of correct calls on the GLM tool-result prompt. Many recovered responses hit a separate argument bug (see Limitations).

## Validation

### Unit tests

New tests:

- `test_inclusive_reasoning_end_token` in `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py`. It runs the validate, bitmask and accept flow with drafts

title: [Bug]: cudagraph_mode=FULL crashes on prefill with FlashInfer sparse MLA on SM100
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM main @ `2a52715ef7`, 1× B200 (SM100), Model Runner V2 (`VLLM_USE_V2_MODEL_RUNNER=1`).

### 🐛 Describe the bug

With `cudagraph_mode=FULL` and the FlashInfer sparse MLA backend on SM100 (`FLASHINFER_MLA_SPARSE`), the engine crashes as soon as a prefill chunk replays a FULL CUDA graph. `FULL_AND_PIECEWISE`, the default, works.

`FlashInferMLASparseTRTLLMMetadataBuilder` declares `AttentionCGSupport.ALWAYS` (added in #52783), so `FULL` mode captures FULL graphs for mixed/prefill batches too. Neither MLA prefill backend can replay those:

| MLA prefill backend | Result |
|---|---|
| FlashAttention (default for DeepSeek-V3.2) | `CUDA error: an illegal memory access was encountered` during FULL-graph replay |
| TRTLLM ragged (default for larger MLA dims, e.g. GLM-5.3) | `ValueError: TRTLLM ragged prefill contains mixed active and empty query rows: query_lens=[512, 0, 0, 0]`: the FULL graph pads the batch with empty requests |
| FlashInfer | not valid for these MLA dimensions |

In both failing cases, a 512-token prefill chunk is dispatched to a request-padded FULL graph. The variable-length verification FULL graphs that adaptive DSpark (#52783) needs may be what `ALWAYS` was meant for. If so, a lower support level plus the varlen-decode hook might cover that without capturing prefill.

**Repro** (DeepSeek-V3.2 shrunk to 4 layers, dummy weights; no HiSparse or KV connector). Pass `TRTLLM_RAGGED` or `FLASH_ATTN` as the argument to pick the prefill backend:

title: [Core][Spec Decode] Group sliding-window draft layers separately in the GLM-5.3 builder
bodyExcerpt:
### Summary

GLM-5.3-Flash (`glm5_next`) fails to start with any EAGLE-family drafter whose layers are plain sliding-window attention (e.g. the block-diffusion DFlash2 drafter, 5 GQA `SlidingWindowSpec` layers). `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` only accepts exact `MLAAttentionSpec` in the attention group, so it declines; the generic page-size unification then cannot pad the DSA indexer (MLA family) and startup dies:

```
NotImplementedError: indexer.k_cache: page size is not divisible by the maximum
page size and cannot be padded. Padding is only supported for non-MLA attention layers
```

This is the same direction as the draft-group work in #58638 (KV cache grouping for hybrid models with speculative drafters), applied to the GLM-5.3 builder, which was not covered there.

### Root cause

`_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` builds one packed group for `MLAAttentionSpec` + indexer (MLA with `tokens_per_state > 1`) layers and aliases the kpool tails onto the indexer tensors. Its gate requires every non-Mamba / non-`KpoolTailSpec` spec to be exactly `MLAAttentionSpec`. A drafter contributes uniform `SlidingWindowSpec` layers with the draft worker's own (small) block size, so the gate returns `None`. The generic `unify_kv_cache_spec_page_size` then tries to pad every page up to the max (MLA) page; the indexer page is MLA-family and explicitly refuses padding, so `get_kv_cache_groups` raises.

### Changes

One file, `vllm/v1/core/kv_cache_utils.py`:

- `_get_kv_cache_groups_glm5_next` splits `HiddenStateCacheSpec` (aux-eagle) and uniform drafter `SlidingWindowSpec` layers (excluding `KpoolTailSpec` / sliding-window MLA) out of `attn_specs`; the strict all-MLA gate now only applies to the target's attention layers. Absorbing the extras requires `speculative_config.use_eagle()`.
- Draft layers get their own `KVCacheGroupSpec`, re-aligned to the target block size (the packed GLM layout needs a single LCM / scheduler block), with `is_eagle_group=use_eagle_b

title: [Bugfix][MRV2] Keep GDN prefill checkpoint metadata local to each cache group
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

In the GLM-5.3-Flash configuration we tested with Model Runner V2 (MRV2) and prefix caching, later requests could return garbled output despite succeeding. A **checkpoint**—attention state saved for prefix reuse—could be written to the wrong cache page. Found while testing [providers-verifier](https://github.com/smg-project/providers-verifier).

## Claims

- The [two-line fix](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L129-L139) makes checkpoint configurations use the runner's [existing per-group metadata construction](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/worker/gpu/attn_utils.py#L523-L548).
- Configurations without checkpoint blocks still reuse metadata.
- Prefix caching and GLM's internal prefill checkpoint optimization from #56960 remain enabled: a full prefill can save an intermediate checkpoint without an extra model forward when the token budget permits.

## Validation

### Minimal reproducible example

Each **KV cache group** has its own cache-page mapping. When switching groups, [`update_block_table()`](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/blob/df28422b4d5be9314388a971952bdc614e13a292/vllm/v1/attention/backends/gdn_attn.py#L613-L661) updates the active-state page but retains the previous group's checkpoint page:

| Page for the next cache group | Expected | Actual |
| --- | ---: | ---: |
| Active state | `202` | `202` |
| Checkpoint | `222` | **`111`** |

title: [Bugfix][Structured Outputs] Keep tool-call openers that end reasoning inside the grammar constraint
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Fixes #59608. When reasoning ends on a tool-call opener instead of `</think>` (GLM-4.7/5.x can jump straight from reasoning into `<tool_call>`), the structured-output gate started the grammar constraint one token past the opener. The grammar never saw the opener, so it forced the model to emit a second `<tool_call>`, the parser then dropped the malformed call, and `required`/named tool calls came back empty.

## Claims

- The reasoning-end fast path now distinguishes terminators that are pure reasoning syntax (`</think>`) from terminators that are the first content token (a tool-call opener), using the transition events already declared in each parser config.
- For content terminators the constraint starts at the marker and the marker is fed to the grammar, so the grammar state advances past the opener instead of re-forcing it. Pure terminators keep the existing `offset + 1` behavior.
- Configs affected on main: `glm47_moe` (the `glm45`/`glm47` reasoning parsers), `qwen3`, `gemma4`, `mistral`. Each has a `(REASONING, tool opener)` transition that emits both `REASONING_END` and `TOOL_CALL_START` on a single-token terminal.

## Validation

New unit coverage, all runnable on CPU:

- `tests/parser/engine/test_glm47_moe.py`: the GLM config derives `reasoning_end_token_ids == {</think>, <tool_call>}` and `reasoning_end_content_token_ids == {<tool_call>}`.
- `tests/parser/engine/test_deepseek_v4.py`: the multi-token DSML opener stays out of both sets (negative case).
- `tests/v1/structured_output/test_structured_output_manager.py`: manager-level flows with real xgrammar/guidance/outlines grammars. Under a `z[0-9]+` regex with `z` as a content terminator, the marker row is constrained (`UCCC`, was `UUCC`), the grammar consumes the marker on accept, and afterwards a digit validates while a duplicate marker is rejected. A companion case locks the pure-marker path through the same fast-path branch (`UUCCC`, unchanged).

title: [ROCm] Enable DeepSeek-V3.2 / GLM-5.3 sparse MLA on gfx11
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

DeepSeek-V3.2 and GLM-5.3 don't start on gfx11. Every worker dies with:

```
RuntimeError: Worker failed with error ''_OpNamespace' 'vllm' object has no
attribute 'rocm_aiter_mla_decode_fwd'', please check the stack trace above for
the root cause
```

For sparse MLA, `ROCM_AITER_MLA_SPARSE` is the only backend on offer, and it
needs AITER's MLA assembly kernels, which have no gfx11 build. The Triton
sparse path in the same file already handles the 512 + 64 RoPE layout, but
`_use_rocm_sparse_triton()` only picks it when `head_size == kv_lora_rank`.

This PR lets gfx11 take that path too. Same idea as #47017, which unblocked
DeepSeek-V4 on gfx11. fp8 KV cache still goes to AITER.

Tests: one new routing test for the gfx11 case, and the existing routing test
now pins `on_gfx11` to `False` so it also passes on gfx11 hardware.

## Duplicate-work check

Searched open PRs and issues for `rocm_aiter_mla_decode_fwd`, GLM-5.3 and
DeepSeek-V3.2 on gfx11, and sparse MLA fallback on ROCm. No duplicate. One
open PR is adjacent but distinct:

- #52970 (`officially supporting aiter Triton kernels+dsv4 on RDNA3`) is about
  DeepSeek-V4 and AITER's Triton kernels. It does not touch
  `_use_rocm_sparse_triton`.

## Test Result

Tested on 4x Strix Halo / Radeon 8060S / gfx1151 with `TP=4`, ROCm 7.14.

title: [Bugfix][Parser] Retain reasoning token counts across empty text deltas
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Preserve reasoning-token usage when incremental detokenization produces empty text. For example, a byte-fallback tokenizer emits `中` from three token IDs, but streaming parsing currently reports one reasoning token while batch parsing reports three.

## Claims

- Retain ordinary token counts across empty deltas and stop-string buffering, assigning them after the surrounding control boundaries resolve.
- Preserve count-only prefixes and tails when deferred special-token boundaries resolve or flush.
- Keep byte tokens inside text-based control markers out of reasoning usage.

## Validation

The 59 added cases use a local Hugging Face ByteFallback tokenizer and the production vLLM incremental detokenizer, plus focused scanner checks. They cover DeepSeek V4, Qwen3, GLM4.7, a DeepSeek V4.1 text-tool boundary, several token batch sizes and stop-buffer holdbacks, incomplete UTF-8, and deferred THINK_END/DROP markers. **43 fail and 16 controls pass on the unchanged base; all 59 pass after the patch.**

```bash
python -m pytest --confcutdir=tests/parser/engine tests/parser/engine -q
```

Result: **5,397 passed** on macOS arm64 CPU. Full pre-commit hooks, including mypy and test CI tethering, passed. An exact-base corpus comparison matched all 174 existing samples in batch and three streaming modes: **696 matching outputs and reasoning counts across 15 formats**.

The run used local tokenizer fixtures and excluded top-level GPU fixtures. A source-checkout version warning was present. No GPU, model inference, or live-server validation was performed.

## Details

The scanner previously discarded ordinary IDs when their incremental text was empty. Counting them immediately in the current state is insufficient: a detokenizer can buffer both text and a control boundary. The scanner now carries counts on the appropriate side of deferred markers, and the lexer holds count-only input until subsequent text or a flush determines whether it belongs to content or a text cont

title: [Bug]: GLM-5.3-Flash (Glm5Next): common non-square images (4032x3024, 3840x2160, A4 at 300 dpi) are refused with "exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921"
bodyExcerpt:
### Your current environment

vLLM `0.28.1rc1.dev580+g385dce36b` (source commit 385dce36bcee42309924a5ece951a96db3dce7f2), `nvidia/GLM-5.3-Flash-NVFP4` at revision `423acf37583782c51c142d145aef733d72943d93`, two DGX Spark (GB10) nodes, `max_num_batched_tokens` 2048, vision enabled (image only). The sizing code below is unchanged on main as of 4c2d277643e217344056e1d2c42115d5f005912f.

### 🐛 Describe the bug

Valid images that the model's own processor accepts are rejected with HTTP 400:

```
The decoder prompt contains a(n) image item with 7950 embedding tokens, which exceeds the pre-allocated encoder cache size 7921. Please reduce the input size or increase the encoder cache size by setting --limit-mm-per-prompt at startup.
```

It is deterministic and it hits ordinary images. A typical phone photo (4032×3024), a 4K frame (3840×2160) and an A4 page at 300 dpi (3508×2480) all fail, while a square image of nearly the same size passes. Reproduced with generated images (script below), one request per image, `max_tokens` 8; the same seven results on two serving configurations:

| image | HTTP | tokens |
|---|---|---|
| 2560×1440 (QHD) | 200 | prompt 4,802 |
| 3000×3000 (square) | 200 | prompt 7,939 |
| 5000×2000 | 200 | prompt 7,858 |
| 4032×3024 (phone photo, 4:3) | **400** | image item 7,931 |
| 3840×2160 (4K, 16:9) | **400** | image item 7,973 |
| 3508×2480 (A4 at 300 dpi) | **400** | image item 7,950 |
| 2600×2400 | **400** | image item 7,998 |

(The accepted rows' prompt tokens are the image tokens plus 18 text tokens: 4,784, 7,921 and 7,840 image tokens.)

**Cause, as far as I can tell**

- The checkpoint's `processor_config.json` declares `max_image_tokens: 8000`, so the processor budget is `max_pixels = 8000 × 28 × 28 × 2 = 12,544,000`.
- The encoder cache is sized from `get_max_image_tokens()`, which uses `get_image_size_with_most_features()`. `Glm5NextProcessingInfo` (`vllm/models/glm5next/common/multimodal.py`) does not override it, so it inherits `Glm4vProc
author: Bizuayeu

title: [Bugfix] Keep the GLM-5.3 kpool tail and Qwen4 QSA ring out of the null block
bodyExcerpt:
## Purpose

Block id 0 is the null block. It is shared by every KV cache group and is assumed to stay zero. Since #35431, the runners mark rows that own no state with 0 in the block table, not `PAD_SLOT_ID`: dummy runs, CUDA graph capture and padding rows all carry 0. Two ring caches that address their pages through column 0 of the block table did not treat 0 as "no ring", so dummy runs wrote their rows into block 0:

- **GLM-5.3-Flash kpool tail:** `_kpool_tail_slot_mapping_kernel` maps every token to `block_table[req][0] * kpool + pos % kpool`. Its torch fallback does the same.
- **Qwen4 QSA circular ring:** `circular_qsa_slot_mapping` and `_build_qsa_metadata_kernel` map tokens to `block_table[req, 0]` and kept every block `>= 0`. The compressed QSA path already keeps dummy slots inert (`test_qsa_compressed_metadata_keeps_dummy_slots_inert`); the ring path did not.

Every scheduled request owns its ring block, so a request on the null block has none. Its tokens now map to PAD, as the generic slot mapping does. The ring writers already skip PAD slots.

This is the same pattern as #58560, which fixes the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.

## Changes

- `vllm/v1/attention/backends/mla/indexer.py`: the kpool tail slot mapping (Triton and torch) emits PAD for requests on the null block.
- `vllm/models/qwen4_exp/common/qsa_cache.py`: the QSA circular ring slot mapping (torch and Triton) requires block `> 0`.
- Tests: the existing QSA circular metadata test, which runs the Triton builder, also checks a dummy batch (all-zero block table) and expects PAD. QSA tests that used block 0 as a real ring block now start real blocks at 1. This includes `_make_block_table` in the pre-indexer test, which could randomly hand out block 0. The kpool tail change has no new test: its unit tests run the torch fallback on CPU, while production only takes the Triton kernel. It was checked by hand on both paths.

## Not a duplicate

- #58560 covers only the DeepSeek-V4.1 compressor ring.
- #57
author: ivanium

title: [KV Offload] Give each rank its own CPU region outside the replicated layout
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, ranks never read each other's slots, but they still share one region whose rows interleave all ranks. Every rank pre-faults and pins its strided slots in the same shm file, contending with the others.

Give each rank its own region holding only its slots, in its own shm file. No other process maps that file, so the rank no longer waits on the cross-worker barrier before unlinking it. The replicated layout keeps the shared region.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 22.6 s (22.8 and 22.4 s in two runs), and pinning from 20.8 to 3.3 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1182 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.
author: Etelis

title: [KV Offload] Split the CPU offload region across shm files
bodyExcerpt:
Pre-faulting the CPU offload region is capped by its single `/dev/shm` file: page-cache inserts into one shmem file are serialized, so more workers or threads stop helping. On one H200 node, eight processes pre-faulting disjoint parts of a 64 GiB file reach 9.8 GiB/s in total. Given one file each, they reach 24.6 GiB/s, and sixteen files reach 44.8 GiB/s. #59430 hits the same ceiling with threads.

Split the region's rows over up to 32 files of at least 1 GiB each. The files are mapped back to back over one anonymous reservation, so the region stays contiguous. Workers with per-rank slots start pre-faulting on different files. Regions under 2 GiB, and other users of `SharedOffloadRegion`, keep a single file.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 38.3 s, and pre-faulting from 42.8 to 19.4 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1183 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.
author: Etelis

title: [KV Offload] Split replicated-layout pre-faulting across workers
bodyExcerpt:
With the replicated layout, every worker maps the same bytes, yet every worker still pre-faults the whole region. At TP4, that is four passes over one shm file, all contending for the same pages.

Give each worker one contiguous, page-aligned share to pre-fault instead. The pages are shared, so the region still ends up fully populated.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main). GLM-5.3 only uses the replicated layout with #57652, so these runs have that PR applied:

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 162.8 to 46.7 s. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1184 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.
author: Etelis

title: [KV Offload] Pin only each worker's own offload slots
bodyExcerpt:
Outside the replicated layout, each worker only uses its own slot of every row in the shared CPU region, yet every worker `cudaHostRegister`s the whole region. At TP4, every page gets pinned four times.

Register only the worker's slot of each row, rounded out to pages. The replicated layout keeps whole-region registration. So do slots within a page of the full row and regions over 65,536 rows, where per-call overhead would dominate.

TieringOffloadingSpec workers pin through the same path, so they get this too. #59430 lists this redundant pinning as a follow-up, and no open PR changes it.

## Tests

4× H200, measured on `16d4ac4ba3` with this change (the touched files are unchanged on current main):

- GLM-5.3 W4A8, TP4 + EP, 256 GiB native CPU offload: the offload startup step fell from 63.6 to 34.8 s, and pinning from 20.8 to 6.8 s, as each rank registered 68.8 GB instead of 274.9 GB. A 20k-token retrieval prompt answered 8/8 lookups cold and 8/8 after `/reset_prefix_cache`, with 3.9 GB reloaded from CPU.
- `pytest tests/v1/kv_offload tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/offloading_connector tests/v1/kv_connector/unit/test_offloading_connector.py tests/v1/worker/test_utils.py`: 1184 passed. The 7 failing tests need a gated model and fail the same way on main.
- pre-commit, including mypy, passed.

title: [Core] Take the top-k/top-p Triton scratch from WorkspaceManager
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Take the per-program float32 scratch of `apply_top_k_top_p_triton` from `WorkspaceManager`, reserved at its maximum size by the GPU model runners before capture and the workspace lock. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

## Claims

- The sampler scratch (`min(num_sm, batch) × vocab × 4 B`; 77 MiB per GPU on DeepSeek-V4-Flash, 92 MiB on GLM-5.3) no longer stays resident while the engine sleeps once #59156 lands, and no longer grows lazily under traffic after warm-up.
- Kernel behavior is unchanged: the same `(NUM_PROGRAMS, vocab)` float32 buffer is handed to `_topk_topp`.
- Callers without a reservation (CPU, tests, `diffusion_gemma`, the watermark sampler, batches larger than the reservation) keep the module-level cached buffer, so nothing can hit the workspace lock.

## Validation

- Unit tests (H200): `tests/v1/sample/test_topk_topp_sampler.py`, `test_sampler.py`, `test_rejection_sampler.py`: 236 passed, 1 skipped, 7 failed; the 7 failures (`TestFlashInferDistributionMatch`, `No module named 'scipy'`) are identical on unmodified `main` in that environment.
- `pre-commit` (ruff, ruff format, mypy, etc.) passes on the commit.
- End-to-end, DeepSeek-V4-Flash TP4 with MTP, CUDA graphs and `--enable-sleep-mode` on 4× GB300, same image and node, on top of #59156 + #59158 + #59360:
  - Memory per GPU after `/sleep` (nvidia-smi): 6313/6439 MiB without this PR (an earlier 100-cycle run of the same stack on the same node, not a back-to-back A/B), 6023 MiB on all 4 GPUs with it. Only about 75 MiB of that is attributable to this change: torch-allocated memory outside the KV cache drops by 75 MiB (the lazily grown sampler buffer); the rest is caching-allocator reserved space (-162 MiB) and the +126 MiB the baseline shows on two GPUs from run to run.
  - Post-wake parity 0/0/0/0 MiB; 3 sleep/wake cycles (full, selective, full) with 195/195 outputs identical to the pre-sleep reference; no `Workspace is locked` errors.

title: [Core] Move FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces into WorkspaceManager
bodyExcerpt:
## Overview

Move the FlashInfer MLA decode workspaces (sparse trtllm-gen/cute-dsl, dense MLA, DSV4/DSV4.1 sparse) from module-global `torch.zeros` tensors into `WorkspaceManager` scratch. Part of #59055; with #59156 the memory is then released by `/sleep`.

## Claims

- The 394 MiB per GPU FlashInfer sparse-MLA workspace (GLM-5.3 / GLM-5.3-Flash) and the 128/256 MiB dense-MLA and DSV4 workspaces no longer stay resident while the engine sleeps once #59156 lands, and are no longer additive to the shared scratch while awake.
- No behavior change for the kernels: the buffers are requested at the same size, reserved before CUDA graph capture, and re-requested on every call (same pattern as `flashmla_sparse.py`, `prefill/trtllm_ragged.py`).
- The DCP sizing (`_required_workspace_bytes`) and `VLLM_FLASHINFER_WORKSPACE_BUFFER_SIZE` override are unchanged.

## Validation

- Read FlashInfer 0.7.0 (`mla/_core.py`, `data/csrc/trtllm_fmha_kernel_launcher.cu`, `cute_dsl/attention/{mla_decode.py,monolithic/mla_decode.py}`); 0.7.0.post1 (the pinned version) differs from 0.7.0 only in `aot.py`, `jit/gemm/core.py` and tests. On every decode path these backends use, the workspace holds only per-launch scratch (trtllm-gen: softmax-stats slab + split-KV scratch, semaphores live in the separate `multi_ctas_kv_counter_buffer`; cute-dsl: split-KV `acc_o`/`acc_lse` partials consumed by the reduction kernel of the same call; SM120 sparse: `mid_out`/`mid_lse` partials), so no content survives between calls and no zero-init is needed. The prefill backends already hand trtllm-gen an uninitialized `WorkspaceManager` view.
- No other `WorkspaceManager` view is an input/output of these decode kernels on the paths read (inputs come from the persistent `topk_indices_buffer`, the index group, Triton converters, `_mtp_hidden_buffer`).
